title: AST SpaceMobile Stock (ASTS) Falls 8.7% on Q3 Revenue Miss (Nov 10)
summary: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) fell 8.67% to $33.69 on Nov 10 after Q3 revenue missed estimates and its 45-satellite target moved to mid-2027.
body_markdown:
## Why AST SpaceMobile Stock Fell


According to the company's[third-quarter release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001780312/000119312526453758/asts-ex99_1.htm) dated November 9, AST SpaceMobile reported revenue of $42.3 million, up from $14.7 million a year earlier on gateway deliveries and US government milestones, and a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $132.4 million, or $0.44 per share. The company kept its 2026 revenue guidance of $150 million to $200 million and said it is targeting about 45 BlueBird satellites in orbit by mid-2027.


Both headline numbers fell short of expectations, as reported by[Investing.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ast-spacemobile-earnings-analysis-questions-180446708.html) : revenue of $42.32 million compared with an estimate of $47.94 million, and the loss of $0.44 per share compared with an estimate of $0.40. Investing.com also noted that the roughly 45-satellite target had moved from early 2027 to mid-2027. The drop followed[a 14.1% gain on November 9](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/ast-spacemobile-asts-stock-news-november-10-2026/) , per the same report.


Per[The Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/why-ast-spacemobile-plunged-today-215040398.html) , the backdrop mattered more than the quarter: Billy Duberstein tied most of the move to a hotter-than-expected[inflation report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/after-mondays-rally-us-cpi-tonight/) . He wrote that a potential rise in interest rates "disproportionately reduces the present value of AST's future profits," because the company "currently has very little revenue." He also pointed to SpaceX's plan, announced with its June IPO, to pursue direct-to-cell mobile service, which overlaps with AST's business.


## ASTS Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- The company reported cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash of about $3.2 billion as of September 30, 2026, according to its release.
- The release cites $1.0 billion in non-dilutive funding under a J-LEO agreement with Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications and partner Rakuten, plus a US Space Force contract worth about $100 million.
- AST says its commercial ecosystem covers over 60 mobile network operators representing over 3 billion subscribers.


### Risks


- [Simply Wall St.](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/ast-spacemobile-asts-stock-price-231820431.html) noted a trailing 12-month net loss of $628.3 million and fourth-quarter capital spending guidance of $400 million to $500 million, with broad-service revenue pushed out while spending accelerates.
- Per Investing.com, revenue missed estimates in three of the last four quarters, and reaching the low end of 2026 guidance requires roughly $61 million or more in fourth-quarter revenue.
- The Motley Fool flagged SpaceX's direct-to-cell plans as competition and higher interest rates as a pressure on loss-making companies.


Next on the calendar, the company targets nationwide intermittent US service before year-end 2026, while Investing.com lists March 26, 2027 as an estimated, unconfirmed date for fourth-quarter results.
